newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-CORINTHIANS WIN SAO PAULO CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CORINTHIANS WIN SAO PAULO CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Corinthians, who spent nearly $20 million assembling their team, won the Sao Paulo championship on Thursday after drawing 1-1 with Sao Paulo in the tournament's final game.

Corinthians and Sao Paulo finished level on seven points in the four-team final stage but Corinthians took the title by virtue of having the better overall record in the tournament. Both teams had won their first two games in the final stage.
Corinthians, needing just a draw, played cautiously but took the lead on the stroke of halftime through full-back Andre Luiz, who joined them from Sao Paulo at the start of the year.
Seventeen-year-old midfielder Fabio Aurelio headed Sao Paulo's more modest outfit level in the 47th minute.

Sao Paulo played the better football but their strikers Dodo and Colombian Victor Aristizabal, who have scored 35 goals between them in the competition, were kept under wraps by a determined Corinthians defence.
Sao Paulo had defender Bordon sent off in the 74th minute for a second bookable offence.

Corinthians overcame internal bickering during their campaign to win the championship for a record 22nd time and coach Nelsinho Batista is almost certain to leave the club after falling out with the directors.
Former Brazil international Tulio, their most expensive signing at $4.5 million, spent several games on the substitutes' bench, although he still finished as the team's top scorer with 13 goals.
Some reports claimed Tulio's team mates had been jealous at the amount of publicity he received when he arrived at the club and boycotted him.
Palmeiras have won the title 21 times, Sao Paulo 17 and Santos 15.
